components.description: One semester (spring or fall) of relief from up to six credit hours of teaching for a primary-caregiver parent after a birth or adoption, with research, graduate-student work and other responsibilities continuing, at 90% of base salary (10% kept by the department to fund replacement teaching); approval at the University's discretion.
components.mechanism_note: Teaching relief with research and other duties continuing, paid at 90% of base salary: the relief is disproportionate to the pay cut, so it is coded modified_duties with its pay level (R3). The policy calls it 'PCMD leave', but its relief is of teaching, with research and other duties continuing.
components.faculty_group_note: Covered Employees: All Faculty; 'All faculty, both male and female, are eligible for PCMD.'
components.eligible_parent_wording: All faculty, both male and female; due to the birth or adoption of a child; primary caregiver for the newborn or adopted child
components.caregiver_condition_wording: The faculty member must be the primary caregiver for the newborn or adopted child during the period that PCMD is in place. The faculty member will affirm that he/she will be the primary caregiver for the child during the semester in which the PCMD is used.
components.entitlement_note: Approval decides whether there is a benefit: 'may be granted' after a best-interest determination; 'a privilege granted at the University's discretion' (V2). Section 2.6 ('In most cases, the semester requested ... will be approved') concerns which semester is approved, not whether PCMD is granted.
components.duration_note: One semester, spring or fall; 'The leave cannot span over two semesters.' The policy defines its semesters for pay purposes as January 1 - June 30 (spring) and July 1 - December 31 (fall), and also speaks of 'the 16-week semester'. Summer use requires negotiation with the department head and dean and Provost approval (footnote 1).
components.duration_variants: A faculty couple sharing primary care may split PCMD: relief from a total of six credits for the couple, each at 95% of salary during the semester (or two different semesters) each uses it.
components.dual_employee_rule: A faculty couple jointly sharing primary care may split PCMD: relief from a total of six credits for the couple for a semester, each at 95% of salary
components.pay_cap: Not more than the PCMD compensation that, with any outside (grant or contract) compensation, equals 110% of full regular salary for the period of leave
components.relief_note: Relief of up to six credit hours of teaching for the semester (all teaching for a member whose load is six credits or fewer); research, work with graduate students and 'other job responsibilities' continue as stated. Further reduction beyond six credits comes with a commensurate salary cut (c4).
components.time_window: Begins January 1 (spring) or July 1 (fall), no more than 3 months before and no more than 12 months after the expected birth or placement; an adopted child under six, or a special-needs child under 18
components.notice: Formal request on the HR PCMD form as soon as possible; notice to the department head normally no fewer than four months before the expected arrival of the child
components.return_obligation: Return to university service for at least one semester, or repay the salary released (10%) plus any other funding used to cover the teaching assignment

Parental caregiving with modified duties (PCMD) is designed to allow all faculty to request relief of up to six credit hours of teaching for one semester either spring or fall due to the birth or adoption of a child, while continuing to perform other job responsibilities.
time_window: Under this policy, PCMD shall begin January 1 for spring semester and July 1 for fall semester and, no more than three (3) months prior to the expected birth/placement of a child and no more than twelve (12) months following the birth/placement.
An adopted child must be under the age of six or a special needs child under 18 years of age.
dual_employee_rule: A faculty couple jointly sharing responsibility as primary caregivers for a child may split the use of PCMD and each receive relief from a total of six credits for the couple for a semester.
Each faculty member would then receive 95% of their salary during the 16 week semester (or two different semesters) that they use the PCMD policy.
pay_cap: The university shall not be obligated to pay more than the amount of PCMD compensation that, when added to the outside source of compensation, will equal 110% of the faculty member’s full regular salary for the period of leave.
notice: This notice would normally be no fewer than four months prior to the expected arrival of the child; however, it may not be possible to provide this much notice.
return_obligation: The faculty member is obligated to return to university service for at least one semester following the use of PCMD.
runs_concurrently_with: Parental Caregiving with Modified Duties (PCMD) under this policy will run concurrently with FMLA leave (Policy 351 Family and Medical Leave) if applicable.

notes: Reference date 2018-02-26. Policy 366 shows Origin and Effective Date June 23, 2017; the capture is 2020-11-01 and the version note states this is the text in force on the reference date.

PCMD (c1) is the institution's only parental provision in the saved documents: relief from up to six credit hours of teaching for one semester, research and graduate-student work continuing, at 90% of base salary, discretionary. Under R3 a relief with a pay cut is coded part_time_option and is not counted; flagged here as a hard case because the cut is only 10% and funds replacement teaching.
Post-tenure review (Policy 405.12.2) may be postponed for one year if PCMD is used (2.2); recorded here, not as a component: it is not a tenure-clock extension and gives no time off, pay or relief.
Sick or annual leave may not be used in conjunction with PCMD (2.5(3)); no sick-leave terms are saved. Sabbatical and other leave do not affect PCMD eligibility (2.5(4)); not a component.
Administrators in Library and Extension are encouraged to explore making the policy work in their units (366.3); no unit-scope restriction for academic faculty.
Cited but not saved: Policy 351 Family and Medical Leave; Policy 405.1.4(4) and Policy 405.12.2 (Policy 405 is in the folder but not used); the short-term disability leave policy (no title given).

Birth parent chain: PCMD semester (c1, part_time_option at 90%) with the further reduction c4 concurrent in the same semester, or the short-term disability pregnancy portion (c5) in lieu of PCMD; FMLA 12 workweeks (c2) runs alongside PCMD from its start.
Non-birth parent chain: PCMD semester (c1) with c4 concurrent; FMLA 12 workweeks (c2) alongside from its start; c5 does not apply (birth parent only).
